Name: Meikyoku Kissa Violon
Hours: Record time from 12:00, live music some evenings; closed Tuesdays
Address (JA): 東京都杉並区阿佐谷北2-9-5
Notes: A small, intimate classical listening café in a house on a quiet lane, 300 m from JR Asagaya Station, here since 1980. Vinyl in the afternoon, occasional live music in the evening; entry is about ¥500 with coffee. Quieter and less touristy than Lion.

Name: Koga Shoten
Address (JA): ~東京都千代田区神田神保町2丁目
Notes: Used bookshop in the Jimbocho book district specializing in classical scores, composer biographies and music theory. Great for browsing out-of-print editions.

Name: Yamaha Ginza
Notes: Yamaha's 14-floor flagship, with a large sheet-music selection. Anyone can play the ground-floor piano, no booking needed. Yamaha Hall on 7F (333 seats, all wood) holds concerts; check its calendar for your dates.

Name: Academia Music
Notes: Tokyo's specialist for imported classical scores (Henle, Bärenreiter and others), founded in 1947.

Name: Sumida Triphony Hall
Notes: December is "Daiku" (Beethoven's 9th) season in Japan, and NJP with Yutaka Sado plays it here at a Christmas concert and a family concert. They play Tokyo Opera City on Dec 21 too; the Dec 19 (Suntory Hall) and Dec 20 performances are sold out.

Name: Tokyo Opera City Concert Hall
Notes: December is "Daiku" (Beethoven's 9th) season in Japan, and NJP with Yutaka Sado plays it here. They also play Sumida Triphony Hall on Dec 17 and 18; the Dec 19 (Suntory Hall) and Dec 20 performances are sold out.

Name: Francois Kissashitsu
Address (JA): 京都府京都市下京区西木屋町通四条下ル船頭町184
Notes: A historic 1934 café with a baroque ship-cabin interior and classical music playing; it's a registered cultural property. An easy stop downtown, and cash only.

Name: Meikyoku Kissa Ryugetsudo
Address (JA): ~京都府京都市左京区田中上柳町
Notes: A Lion-style silent listening room with a huge record library: request a piece by writing down its catalog number. There's a harpsichord and a piano, and a ¥500 music charge on top of your drink.

Name: Ongaku Kissa Musik
Notes: A 15-seat café opened in 1987 by a former classical-music agency staffer, with Tannoy speakers, a turntable that plays SP records (old 78s), and siphon coffee. Its hours are short, so plan around them.

Name: Montage
Notes: A listening café for baroque and classical records, with a harpsichord and piano on site. It hosts concerts, and on some rehearsal days the café stays open alongside them.

Name: JEUGIA Sanjo Honten
Notes: Kyoto's main music store: CDs and records on 1F, sheet music and music books on 2F, pianos on 4F. Tax-free shopping, five minutes from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Station.

Name: Shimamura Music Grand Front Osaka
Notes: Large sheet music section: classical and imported piano scores, orchestral pocket scores, theory books and composer biographies. Right by Osaka Station.
